items.title: Final Fantasy 14 fans discover "Creepypasta Backrooms" area in Patch 7.55, and Square Enix is feeding into the horror: "If you're not careful and you noclip out of reality..."
items.content:
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Square Enix) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Final Fantasy 14 is no horror game, standing as the MMORPG gem of Square Enix 's beloved JRPG series – but it sure does have its spooky moments.

If you know the lore behind the Palace of the Dead, you're probably familiar with how creepy Final Fantasy 14 can get – but its environments and atmosphere are arguably not very eerie, even in Deep Dungeons with heart-wrenching backstories like PotD… most of them, anyway. One Warrior of Light has discovered an area that almost feels like it should be out-of-bounds in the North Horn of the Occult Crescent, and it's spine-chilling.

"I think I found one of the creepiest places SE did in a while," they write, sharing screenshots of their discovery over on Reddit . The spot comes from the MMO's recent Patch 7.55, and appears after players go through a foggy Silent Hill-esque hole in the wall – yes, hole. "Was wandering in Occult Crescent North Horn and found a hole in the wall and got a big chill in the spine seeing this," as the poster reports.

"Reminded me of some Creepypasta Backrooms shenanigans," they add – and, yeah, I can certainly see why. Everything is paint-white, floating against a pitch-black background. There are crawling arms reaching for nothing, forming freaky arches. Enemies prowl the strange area in the Occult Crescent, too, which commenters note are formidable foes. "I visited there today too, and let's just say it's really risky," as one reply reads. "All enemies are rank 40+," the person responding notes – but there are "four silver chests and a survey point inside" to make it worth it.

If you're not careful and you noclip out of reality in the wrong areas, you'll end up in the… https://t.co/OwasiVpnS9 July 29, 2026

Amusingly, Square Enix has chimed in with its own amusing comment on the matter as well, writing in its own post , "If you're not careful and you noclip out of reality in the wrong areas, you'll end up in the…" It's a silly little reference to the Backrooms, but I love it.

Another Final Fantasy 14 mod goes down following concerns of stalking in the MMO Final Fantasy 14 hit with another stalking mod, not even 2 weeks after the MMO's last one shut down Final Fantasy 14 players demand minion of chonky patch 7.5 boss, and there's hope as Square Enix joins in: "Chort" Will I explore the area for myself? Honestly, I'm not sure I can be bothered tackling the normal part of the Occult Crescent – but the new Phantom weapon does beckon… Final Fantasy 14 is great and all, but Yoshi-P would "tackle completely new game designs and values" if he were to make another MMO.

items.title: This Week in Games - Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold's New Stuff Is Pretty Cool
items.summary: Updates! Updates for everyone - as long as
items.content:
Welcome back, folks! Like many people, I've been keeping my ears open regarding the new Project R.E.D. series, Kakusei Hunter Omegahorn . It's very unique as a tokusatsu series; our protagonist summons giant kaiju to fight each other, while summoning other kaiju (and his spaceship) to serve as extra weapons. It's extremely unlike what you'd expect from Super Sentai or even Kamen Rider , more like a very sci-fi take on Monster Hunter . The Egogears even have faux- Monster Hunter -esque artwork depicting the kaiju on them. Folks were pretty down on Gavan Infinity for a variety of reasons. It's way too soon to say if Omegahorn will also leave folks feeling cold, but kudos to Toei : they're swinging for the fences. Now if only they'd actually stream it in America like with Ultraman ! Come on, even Kamen Rider streams on YouTube via Tokushoutsu!

By the time this column goes live, Monolith Soft's update patch for Xenoblade Chronicles 2 will go live. This'll update the game to run at a clean 60 frames per second and render at 4K resolution in handheld mode. Yes, Virginia, Xenoblade Chronicles 2 will be a real video game now! (I snark, but as much as I love Xenoblade 2 , even I have to admit that it is rough going on the Switch—these updates are sorely needed.) There's a lot more going on than just the textures and rendering, though, so let's talk about it.

 

To get folks who've never played it up to speed, Xenoblade Chronicles 2 is the story of a young relic hunter named Rex who finds himself bound to a legendary living weapon (a Blade) named Pyra, who asks for his help in scaling the legendary World Tree in pursuit of the Architect, the deity who created their world of Alrest. Also, there's a catgirl with a Welsh accent tagging along. It's a great RPG, and if any other game featured a character with Pyra's (and her sister Mythra's) writing, people would still be raving about her character—which is why people really love Pyra and Mythra.

The updates add several features to expand on the base game, on top of all of the other DLC that has been added. First, a new mode called Merc Assault. Xenoblade 2 already had a mercenary mode where you could deploy your spare Blades on missions. Unfortunately, you never really controlled your Blades. While every rare Blade was effectively a character unto themselves, drawn by a known anime artist (featuring renowned names like the late Takahiro Kimura to recent favorites like Shunya Yamashita ), they were basically support characters, literally standing on the sidelines offering magical moral support while your actual party members did the fighting. Merc Assault allows you to actually control your Blades while fighting monsters, with their skills and elements combining in unique ways. Chances are, you'll have a great variety of the rare Blades in your party, so you'll have plenty of opportunities to mix and match 'em. And you'll probably even get a lot of mileage out of the Blades you don't normally get to use (alas, poor Gorg). There's also a nifty feature for accessing your Blades' various on-field abilities without equipping them. This is very technical, but trust me: it's a tremendous quality-of-life decision. Gathering items is so much faster now .

Xenoblade 2 's Blades were the main highlight of the game; Monolith Soft designed them to be acquired through an in-game gacha system where you'd spawn them from Core Crystals. No real money was needed, just time and effort in locating the Crystals. There was an in-game reason for all of this, and it even tied into a major twist in the game—but the Doylist reasoning behind it all was that the Switch 2 had media-sharing capabilities that allowed you to share screenshots to Twitter , and Monolith wanted to capitalize upon people's excitement at landing rare acquisitions. Besides the headache of rolling for random Blades, the biggest issue with Blades is that they're all so inconsistently designed. As I understand, there was little direction towards the guest artists regarding how Blades should look. While on the one hand, it helps sell the idea of Blades as bizarre synthetic lifeforms (which, again, ties into plot), it also means that some Blades don't even look like they belong in the same universe as the rest. Still, there's merit to a cast full of freaks—you're bound to find one weirdo you love, and their story is bound to tug at your heartstrings.

Speaking of Blades, protagonists Pyra and Mythra (long story) get new duds as rewards for the new Merc Assault mode... or for scanning their respective Amiibo. The outfits still evoke the normal bits of Pyra's and Mythra's regular outfits, like Pyra's crop top and shorts or Mythra's apron-dress. But I like that the outfits are more consistent between the two of them, reflecting the girls as being two parts of the same whole. The "starry" texture on their clothing also helps give them a more "otherworldly" look, as befitting other rare Blades. And the outfits make the two look a bit more in line with Pneuma. If anything, I miss Pyra's and Mythra's hair looking more saturated—Mythra's faded blond looks more like Pneuma's green, but Pyra looks like she needs to touch up her dye. It's a shame these outfits came out as late as they did; they'd be absolutely sick in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate . I have to wonder if artist Masatsugu Saitō was a little inspired by his work on the upcoming Expelled from Paradise sequel...

Finally, a new Blade was added to Xenoblade Chronicles 2 , and she's a doozy. A lot of people held out hope that Malos, the villain of Xenoblade 2 , would become playable. No such luck. People also hoped that Mythra's descendant would be introduced, since we've met Pyra's and Nia's kids in Xenoblade Chronicles 3 . Also not the case! The new Blade is instead Multiple Observative Mimetic Organicus—or M.O.M.O. for short. M.O.M.O. is from the Xenosaga games, like KOS-MOS: a Realian (synthetic lifeform) designed for communicating with the alien Gnosis. M.O.M.O. has a unique gimmick, where she can swap between two forms: her Real Mode (pictured above) and her "Imaginary Mode," which gives some parts of her skin a transparent crystalline look that reveals her robotic skeleton. While I've lost the tweet that explains this, there's lore behind this: her Imaginary form has an Omega symbol on her forehead that evokes KOS-MOS' design in Xenosaga 2 , and is also meant to interact with Imaginary Space. I'd explain what that means with a smile on my face—but I never got a chance to play Xenosaga (even though I had all three games for my PS2 at one point!). Best I can gather is, there's a lot of technobabble that prevents ordinary humans from engaging with the dangerous Gnosis, and M.O.M.O. is a living robot/computer that facilitates that for them.

Now, I've already mentioned Xenosaga 's beloved gynoid weapons platform Kosmos Obey Strategical Multiple Operation System (KOS-MOS for short). Famously, she was also a rare Blade in Xenoblade 2 —the rarest one, in fact. Her evil duplicate T-ELOS is also around. And as it would happen, events in Xenoblade 3 imply that KOS-MOS and the rest of Xenosaga are, to some extent, canon to Xenoblade . Yes, that would include Mary Magdalene. Tetsuya Takahashi and Soraya Soga are like that. But let's not pay attention to the wrong part of the story. M.O.M.O.'s presence brought a detail that has Xenoblade and Xenosaga fans abuzz. When KOS-MOS was included in Xenoblade 2 , the game's copyright information included Bandai Namco, who famously owned the rights to Xenosaga . This, like many other things from Bandai Namco, was a bugbear for a lot of fans, because fans have wanted ports or re-releases of the Xenosaga trilogy for a long time, especially now that Xenoblade has made the overall Perfect Works games much more popular. As you can surmise from my tone, Bandai Namco hasn't really done much about that. But! M.O.M.O.'s presence in Xenoblade 2 doesn't include Bandai Namco's copyright info! A lot of people take this to mean that Nintendo , who currently owns Monolith Soft, has bought out the rights to Xenosaga , and the possibility of a remake is all but inevitable. I'm... not so convinced. Sure, Xenosaga no longer appears on Bandai Namco's list of IPs , but according to sleuths on Reddit, Bandai Namco's trademark on Xenosaga is still valid through 2030 . Moreover, G-MODE 's Xenosaga: Pied Piper release still lists Bandai Namco in its copyright information . This isn't nothing , but I'm not quite going to start jumping for joy just yet. As usual, my stance on rumors is that a rumor and US$3 is good for buying you one cup of coffee. If and when there's actual confirmation from Nintendo one way or another, then we can talk about Xenosaga being back. A company taking out a trademark or a trademark lapsing is sometimes just paperwork and not a sign that a new Chrono Trigger is being worked on. So let's not count turkeys before they hatch. Of course: I'd be down for Xenosaga to come back. It'll be interesting to see how much of it aligns with Xenoblade after all these years. Also, do our friends in Brazil a solid and translate the Xenoblade games into Portuguese, please?

Final Fantasy XIV EU Fanfest was this past weekend in Belgium, and we've got a real doozy of news that came in regarding the critically-acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV, which has an expanded free trial where you can play through the entirety of A Realm Reborn and the award-winning Shadowbringers expansion up to level 80 for free with no restrictions on playtime. No updates yet regarding the aforementioned free trial, so no need to update the copypasta just yet, but there's plenty of other stuff.

Let's get ahead of the 8-ball with this: there's some concern over the expansion because this one is going to have two raids that are effectively crossover media: the first being the Ghosts of Desire alliance raids, which are a crossover with Neon Genesis Evangelion , and the Beyond the Lifestream raid series, which are for the Final Fantasy VII remakes. And yes, the latter means actual battles with named Final Fantasy VII villain, Sephiroth. Licensed content in Final Fantasy VII isn't new , strictly speaking; there have been in-game events featuring outside media like Dragon Quest and Yōkai Watch (heck, the Yōkai Watch event is currently being re-run as we speak!). And there is also a series of in-game raids in the Shadowbringers expansion that are not only NieR: Automata -themed, but even canon to NieR:Automata. But there being two sets of licensed raids in Evercold has folks worried that the story in Evercold is going to suffer, given that Raids tend to be opportunities to expand on stories or in-game lore.

I'm not as worried about the Evangelion crossover raids. The Final Fantasy XIV fanbase skews far older than, say, Goddess of Victory: NIKKE , which also had a pair of Evangelion collaborations that did very badly . But also, your average teenybopper playing NIKKE is too young to really care much about Eva . Jokes abound about FF14 being a fandom retirement home of sorts, but there's a not-insignificant chunk of that game's fandom that is in their 30s, pushing 40. We'll all be going ga-ga dragging our WoLs through fields of abject misery for a single crumpled Orchestrion scroll with a single scribble of Misato on it. (Also, consider: unisex plugsuit outfits.) It's the Final Fantasy VII collab that also has me a bit worried. Now, I know what you're thinking: Final Fantasy XIV is chock-a-block with references to other Final Fantasy games. One of the first mounts you can actually get is a Magitech walker, and it even plays an arrangement of Terra's theme from Final Fantasy VI . Endwalker partially took place on the Moon (as in, the Moon in the sky), and as such took the opportunity to make some choice references to Final Fantasy IV , which also included some lunar adventures. This included an honest-to-God Lunar Whale mount (an older buddy of mine was very taken with that). Long-running Final Fantasy boss Gilgamesh has made numerous appearances in FF14 . So has the Cloud of Darkness, a variety of weapons, Final Fantasy XV 's Noctis, and many others. Heck, the current expansion for Dawntrail features Kefka from Final Fantasy VI . So why is Sephiroth any different?

Barret and Tifa outfits are coming to FF14! pic.twitter.com/9EtZVivgIk

I think part of it is because the iconography of Final Fantasy 7 is so iconic that Final Fantasy VII is practically a different series unto itself even within the umbrella that is Final Fantasy —heck, FF7 has enough spin-offs for it! (Let's see, Before Crisis , Crisis Core , Dirge of Cerberus , Ever Crisis —the spin-offs have a convenient naming scheme...) The Cloud of Darkness or the Ultima Weapon can be handwaved away as just a creative reinterpretation of a known Final Fantasy boss. Sephiroth is Sephiroth . And with Final Fantasy VII being as complicated as it is (especially with the remakes fully embracing extended lore from the rest of the Compilation of Final Fantasy VII ), there's likely some anxiety over things getting even more convoluted for the game. I don't have a solution to this! My only condolence is that people will be able to get Tifa's outfit (and Barret's outfit). Tifa's crop top will hit the glamor plates as hard as 2B's stockings did .

items.title: New Austin convention celebrates Final Fantasy fandom
Final Fantasy 14 could finally introduce a controversial feature to welcome new players
items.summary: Square Enix is finally considering making the hundreds of hours of story easier for new players
items.content:
Listen Thread 6 Add Us Link copied to clipboard By Willa Rowe Published Jul 29, 2026, 2:49 PM EDT News Producer Naoki Yoshida says the team is considering ways to make the lengthy story easier

FFXIV Evercold will finally modernize some of the MMO's most outdated features Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's director can't promise a physical release, but he wants it Despite Magic's unprecedented success, Wizards' president is already stepping down Final Fantasy 14 could finally introduce a controversial feature to welcome new players Photo: Square Enix Final Fantasy 14 Sign in to your Polygon.com account It is becoming increasingly difficult to recommend Final Fantasy 14 to new players as the years go on. Now in its 13th year of service with a sixth expansion due in January, the MMORPG requires hundreds of hours to complete — and that's if we are just talking about the main story. Despite this Herculean effort, Square Enix has been adamant that players must go through the entire game's story to access the latest content. That could finally be changing.

During a media Q&A at Final Fantasy Fan Fest in Berlin (as reported by PC Gamer ), Final Fantasy 14 producer Naoki Yoshida revealed the development team is working on potential solutions to make the game more accessible to beginners. "I had previously said that I want players to enjoy the story, so I would like them to have a fresh experience right from A Realm Reborn ," Yoshida admitted "But now we are at this point, we've begun thinking about accommodating these kinds of requests."

Yoshida shared that Square Enix is considering two ways to address the issue, though he remained fairly cryptic on both. He said that the first one will be implemented before or at Evercold 's release. He teased that the second solution involves a system whose feasibility the development team is in the process of reviewing. "There's a non-zero possibility of us being able to implement it for [patch] 8.0. So there is a possibility that we could make it," Yoshida said.

While the topic of a streamlined path or skip through Final Fantasy 14 's story remains controversial among the fanbase, it makes sense for Square Enix to consider it at this point in the MMO's life. Evercold , the game's next expansion, marks the start of the Godless Realms Saga. This is something of a new beginning, with the MMO's initial story wrapping up in 2021's Endwalker . It has the potential to be the perfect onboarding point for beginners who have, until now, been intimidated by the game's mountain of quests.

Square Enix has already trimmed the lengthy list of main scenario quests over the years in an attempt to make catching up with Final Fantasy 14 easier, but even this has failed to keep pace with the volume of new story content each expansion adds. There are paid story skips available to players for each expansion, but Square Enix seems ready to consider a free implementation of something similar going forward.

One of the biggest concerns with offering players the ability to jump right in to the latest expansion is how it will affect the rest of the player-base. While the story is important, the hours of playtime it takes to get through it also help players learn just how Final Fantasy 14 's mechanics work. As content still revolves around teaming up with other players, 'the community worries that an influx of players without proper tutorials could harm everyone's experience. Yoshida hinted that more details on potential solutions could come during Tokyo Fan Fest in October.

Once more, a horde of Yo-kai descends upon Eorzea! Join in the fun and get your paws on weapons, mounts, a framer's kit, and minions─including Jibanyan and Whisper! This time around, the event features three new indoor furnishings: wibbly-wobbly Jibanyan, wibbly-wobbly Komasan, and wibbly-wobbly USApyon. * This event is identical to the one previously held, with the addition of three indoor furnishing items. * If you have already completed the quest for this event, it cannot be accepted again. Event Duration

From Tuesday, August 4, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 9:00 (BST) / 18:00 (AEST) to Monday, October 5, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. (PDT) / 14:59 (GMT) / 15:59 (BST) / Tuesday, 6 October at 1:59 (AEDT) * Dates and times are subject to change.

How to Participate

Speak with the poor-heeled youth on the Steps of Nald (X:9.2 Y:9.1) in Ul'dah. items.title: Final Fantasy 14′ s Next Expansion Will Feature A Crossover With Final Fantasy 7 So Of Course Fans Are Gonna Fight About It
items.summary: Am I tired of FF7? Yes. Am I still gonna try raiding for the first time just to see this content? Also yes.
items.content:
The conclusion of the Final Fantasy XIV Fan Fest in Berlin brought with it a lot of new updates for Evercold , the game’s upcoming expansion due in January of next year. We got new information on one of the expansion’s two new classes, more details on the story and tweaks to the game’s battle and questing systems, and all the ways players will be able to customize their characters because of course, glamour is the endgame. And one particular announcement—that Evercold ‘s raid series will be a crossover with Final Fantasy VII Remake— has the fandom up in arms.

Presenting a FINAL FANTASY XIV x FINAL FANTASY VII Remake crossover: Beyond the Lifestream—the Evercold raid series developed in collaboration with @finalfantasyvii ! pic.twitter.com/wzkPKFpQky

— FINAL FANTASY XIV (@FF_XIV_EN) July 25, 2026

On the one hand, I get it. Final Fantasy fans have been inundated with this one iteration of Square Enix’s storied franchise for decades now, even before the remake trilogy kicked off back in 2020. And as exciting as that remake trilogy is, I’m kinda tired of seeing Cloud’s ass, too. If I played Final Fantasy XIV to get away from all that, I’d be pissed like some fans are.

Having both raid series be crossovers is very overkill. Why must i go and watch a boring anime and a play 3 new RPG games costing upwards of £150 total to understand the raids in my MMO?

I hope the expansion after Evercold has 2 original raid series to make up for this!

— 「 Xavier Maganti 」 (@JamieCharlesEl1) July 25, 2026

Collabing on BOTH raid types right at the start of what is supposed to be a new storyline is definitely a choice What a wasted opportunity to start adding new lore pic.twitter.com/m2gXqK8WPq

— 🗡️🐍RedPanda 🇪🇭 🇵🇸 (@Surgiote) July 25, 2026

People are saying folks who don't dig this should shut up because XIV is full of references, but no other game in this franchise is pushed remotely as much as VII is. It's reasonable for some people to not be hyped for more.

And man… not everything has to be an argument. It's just opinions.

— Bex (@bexthecat.bsky.social) 2026-07-25T15:26:16.645Z

There’s also a lingering sentiment among players that holding a crossover with the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy now (rather than having one earlier in the trilogy’s lifecycle) is a sly attempt to win back lapsed players or earn new ones who are in the FF ecosystem but never dabbled in the MMO. A lot of players checked out of the game during Dawntrail , the most recent expansion whose story was just not as strong as those of previous expansions (following up Endwalker was always gonna be tough) and adding stuff from the big daddy Final Fantasy entry to the MMO certainly feels like an “in case of emergency, break glass” scenario.

And it’s almost certainly gonna work, too, because for as much as I don’t wanna see Sephiroth’s 34-inch white-blonde buss down on my screen anymore, I will show up for a chance to hear composer Masayoshi Soken’s take on One Winged Angel.

items.title: New FFXIV Twitch Support-a-Streamer Mount Is a Unicorn
items.summary: The FFXIV Twitch Support-a-Streamer promotion is back and this time Alsvid the unicorn mount is the reward.
items.content:
Square Enix announced a new Twitch Support-a-Streamer FFXIV promotion that gives players a chance to buy and gift qualifying subscriptions in order to earn an Alsvid Whistle to summon a new rainbow unicorn mount. It kicked off on July 28, 2026. People will have until August 25, 2026 to earn the Mog Station code for the item, and they need to have an active account to redeem the code.

The Twitch promotion only applies to streams in the FFXIV category on the service and Affiliate and Partner channels streaming the game while that stream is set to the correct category. You then need to buy three subscriptions. These can be tier 1, 2, or 3 ones that you either get for yourself or choose to gift.

After you buy the three applicable subscriptions, you will get the FFXIV Alsvid unicorn mount code in your Twitch Notifications Inbox. Only one code can be earned per promotion. Said Item Code can be redeemed in Mog Station in Registration Codes.

To go along with the reveal, Square Enix also shared two in-game screenshots of the mount being used.

This sort of FFXIV Twitch Support-a-Streamer promotion happened before. In 2024, it ended up being the way to get the Snowstreamer Snowman mount.

Final Fantasy XIV is on the PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X, and PC now, comes to the Switch 2 on August 4, 2026, and FFXIV Evercold will appear in January 2027. The FFXIV Twitch Support-a-Streamer Alsvid the unicorn mount promotion will run between July 28, 2026 and August 25, 2026.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Online Releases For Switch 2 On 4th August 2026
items.content:
Earlier this year, Square Enix announced Final Fantasy XIV Online would be making its way to the Switch 2 in August.

Now, in an update , it has confirmed its MMORPG will be launching for Nintendo's new hybrid system on 4th August 2026 . Pre-orders are now available for the following versions on the Switch 2 eShop. There's currently a pre-order discount on select versions.

There will also be the Final Fantasy XIV Online Free Trial . As for game download, the estimated file size is listed as 117GB .

Apart from this, Square Enix has also revealed a Final Fantasy XIV x Final Fantasy VII Remake Evercold raid series and shared trailers for an extended teaser trailer of Evercold , a new job (Bastion), new areas ( Hringhorni & Naglfar ), a new city ( Fargarth ), and the new Final Fantasy XIV x Evangelion crossover.

Players will require a separate subscription from other platforms

items.content:
The Make It Rain Campaign returns once more to the Gold Saucer! With a 50% MGP bonus and an assortment of adorable otter-themed goods on offer, you won't want to miss out! Furthermore, campaign attendants will be offering a range of items at discounted prices, including some exclusive limited-time deals, so be sure to join the festivities and rake in the rewards while you can!

Event Duration

From Friday, May 29, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 9:00 (BST) / 18:00 (AEST) to Wednesday, June 24, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. (PDT) / 14:59 (GMT) / 15:59 (BST) / Thursday, 25 June at 0:59 (AEST)

How to Participate

Begin the quest "You Otter Be There" by speaking to Ollier in Ul’dah - Steps of Nald (X:9.4 Y:9.1). * Players must be level 15 and above to start the quest. * Players must first complete the quest "It Could Happen to You."

Rewards

* MGP rewards from the Gold Saucer have been increased by 50% for the duration of this event. * Certain items available during previous iterations of the event can be obtained via the campaign attendant. * The Crystal Tower striker, Monster Toss machine, Cuff-a-Cur machine, and a number of other prizes may be purchased at a reduced MGP cost from the campaign attendant. Visit the special site for more details.
